title: Kazakh Famine (Asharshylyk) of 1930–1933
note: Devastating famine caused by forced sedentarization and livestock confiscations in Soviet Kazakhstan under Stalin, killing an estimated 1.5 million people (more than one-third of the Kazakh population) and severely under-recorded in global historical surveys.

title: Deportation of the Chechens and Ingush (Operation Chechevitsa)
note: Total forced deportation of the Chechen and Ingush populations to Central Asia ordered by Stalin and Beria in February 1944, recognized by the European Parliament as an act of genocide.

title: Nadezhda Alliluyeva
note: Second wife of Joseph Stalin, revolutionary Bolshevik who worked in Lenin's secretariat and enrolled at the Industrial Academy; her suicide in November 1932 marked a pivotal psychological turning point in Stalin's isolation and cruelty.

title: NKVD Operational Order No. 00447 and Mass Operations
note: The central secret decree of the Great Terror establishing regional quota-based executions and troika tribunals targeting former kulaks, marginals, and political suspects.
